title: Scalable Generation of Mature Cerebellar Organoids from Human Pluripotent Stem Cells and Characterization by Immunostaining
protocol: Thaw the basement membrane matrix stock at 4 °C and prepare 60 μL aliquots.
Freeze the aliquots at -20 °C.
Thaw one aliquot of the basement membrane matrix on ice.
Add 60 µL to 6 mL of DMEM-F12.
Incubate the diluted basement membrane matrix solution in each well of a 6 well plate for at least 1 h at room temperature or store at 4 °C for up to 1 week.
Aspirate the solution from the plate using a serological pipette.
Add 0.5 mL of mTeSR1 medium to each well immediately after aspirating the previous solution.
Aspirate the spent medium from the well containing iPSCs.
Wash once using 1 mL of 0.5 mM EDTA per well.
Incubate the wells with 1 mL of 0.5 mM EDTA for 5 min at room temperature.
Aspirate EDTA from the wells.
Remove cells by adding mTeSR1 medium and pipetting using a P1000 micropipette, gently.
Collect cells in a conical tube.
Add 1 mL of cell suspension diluted 1:4 to each well.
Return cells to an incubator at 5% CO2 and 37 °C.
Replace spent medium daily.
Passage cells every 3 days when they achieve 75%–80% confluence.
Incubate iPSCs grown as monolayers in mTeSR1 supplemented with 10 µM ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 for 1 hour at 37 °C, 95% humidity, and 5% CO2.
Aspirate the spent medium from each well after incubation.
Wash wells once with 1 mL of 1× PBS per well.
Add 1 mL of cell detachment medium to each well of a 6 well plate and incubate at 37 °C for 7 minutes until cells detach easily.
Pipette the cell detachment medium up and down with a P1000 micropipette until cells dissociate into single cells.
Add 2 mL of complete cell culture medium to each well to inactivate enzymatic digestion.
Gently pipette cells into a sterile conical tube.
Centrifuge at 210 × g for 3 minutes and remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in culture medium supplemented with 10 µM ROCKi.
Count the iPSCs using a hemocytometer with trypan blue dye.
Seed 15 × 10^6 single cells in the bioreactor with 60 mL of mTeSR1 supplemented with 10 µM ROCKi at a final density of 250,000 cells/mL.
Place the vessel containing iPSCs in the universal base unit inside an incubator set to 37 °C, 95% humidity, and 5% CO2.
Set the universal base unit control to maintain stirring at 27 rpm for 24 hours.
Collect 1 mL of iPSC aggregates sample on day 1 using a serological pipette.
Maintain bioreactor agitation as before during sample collection.
Plate the cell suspension in an ultra-low attachment 24 well plate.
Check that iPSC-derived aggregates are formed.
Acquire images of the aggregates with an optical microscope at total magnifications of 40x or 100x.
Measure the area of the aggregates using FIJI software.
Select “File | Open” from the menu bar to open a stored image file.
Create a straight line over the scale bar in the image using the line selection tool.
Select “Analyze | Set scale” from the menu bar.
Add the expanse of the image's scale bar in µm as Known distance.
Define the Unit of length as µm.
Click on Global to maintain settings and OK.
Select Oval Selection in the toolbar.
For each aggregate, delineate the area with the oval tool.
Select “Analyze | Measure” from the menu bar.
Calculate their diameter based on measured area, considering aggregates are approximately spherical.
When the average diameter of the aggregates is 100 µm, replace 80% of the spent medium with fresh mTeSR1 without ROCKi.
When aggregates reach 200–250 μm in diameter, replace all the spent medium with gfCDM (Table 1).
If the average aggregate diameter exceeds 350 μm, do not start the differentiation protocol and repeat seeding of single cells.
Insert the bioreactor containing the aggregates into the universal base unit placed in the incubator at 37 °C, 95% humidity, and 5% CO2.
Decrease the bioreactor agitation to 25 rpm.
On day 2, repeat steps for evaluating aggregate diameter.
Add 30 μL of FGF2 (final concentration, 50 ng/mL) and 60 μL of SB431542 (final concentration, 10 μM) to 60 mL of gfCDM differentiation medium.
Replace all spent medium from the bioreactor with supplemented gfCDM.
Repeat step for replacing medium in the bioreactor.
On day 5, repeat steps for evaluating aggregate diameter and other specified steps.
Dilute FGF2 and SB431542 to 2/3 concentration: Add 20 μL of FGF2 and 40 μL of SB431542 to 60 mL of gfCDM differentiation medium.
Replace all spent medium from the bioreactor with supplemented gfCDM.
Increase bioreactor agitation to 30 rpm.
On day 7, repeat steps for evaluating aggregate diameter.
Add 60 μL of FGF19 (final concentration, 100 ng/mL) to 60 mL of gfCDM differentiation medium.
Replace all spent medium from the bioreactor with supplemented gfCDM containing FGF19.
On day 14, repeat steps for evaluating aggregate diameter and other specified steps.
On day 21, repeat steps 3.2, 3.3, and 3.4.
Replace all spent medium from the bioreactor with complete neurobasal medium (Table 1).
Repeat step 3.6.
On day 28, repeat steps 3.2, 3.3, and 3.4.
Add 180 μL of SDF1 (final concentration, 300 ng/mL) to 60 mL of complete neurobasal medium.
Replace all spent medium from the bioreactor with complete neurobasal medium supplemented with SDF1.
Repeat step 3.6.
On day 35, repeat steps 3.2, 3.3, and 3.4.
Replace all spent medium from the bioreactor with complete BrainPhys medium (Table 1).
Repeat step 3.6.
Replace 1/3 of the total volume every 3 days with complete BrainPhys medium until day 90 of differentiation.
Collect 1 mL of sample of medium containing organoids with a serological pipette from the bioreactor to a 15 mL conical tube.
Remove the supernatant and wash once with 1 mL of 1× PBS.
Let the organoids settle by gravity.
Remove the supernatant and add 1 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA).
Incubate at 4 °C for 30 min.
Remove the spent PFA and add 1 mL of 1× PBS.
Store the organoids in 1 mL of 1× PBS at 4 °C until processing for cryosectioning.
Do not store the organoids for more than 1 week after fixation.
Remove the supernatant from the stored organoids.
Add 1 mL of 15% sucrose (w/v, diluted in 1× PBS).
Mix well by gentle swirling and incubate overnight at 4 °C.
Prepare a solution of 15% sucrose/7.5% gelatin and maintain it at 37 °C to avoid solidification.
Remove the 15% sucrose solution from organoids.
Add 1 mL of 15% sucrose/7.5% gelatin to the organoids, mix gently.
Incubate at 37 °C for 1 h.
Add 15% sucrose/7.5% gelatin solution to a plastic container up to half its volume and wait for solidification at room temperature.
After incubation, place a sucrose/gelatin drop containing the organoids on the solidified gelatin with a Pasteur pipette.
Leave to solidify at room temperature for about 15 min, avoiding bubble formation.
Add 15% sucrose/7.5% gelatin solution on top of the organoids until the container is filled and wait for complete solidification at room temperature.
Incubate 20 min at 4 °C after solidification.
Cut the gelatin into a cube containing the organoids in the center.
Fix the gelatin cube on a piece of cardboard with a drop of O.C.T. compound.
Place 250 mL of isopentane in a 500 mL cup and fill an appropriate container with liquid nitrogen.
Cool the isopentane to -80 °C using liquid nitrogen.
When -80 °C is reached, place the gelatin cube into the cup containing isopentane until it freezes.
Store the frozen gelatin cube at -80 °C.
Turn on the cryostat and define both specimen (OT) and cryochamber (CT) temperatures at -25 °C.
Fix the gelatin cube containing organoids on the specimen using O.C.T. compound when both temperatures stabilize.
Define section thickness at 12 µm.
Cut the cube and collect 3–4 slices on adhesion microscope slides.
Store the microscope slides with organoid sections at -20 °C until use.
Place the microscope slides containing organoid sections in a coupling jar with prewarmed 1x PBS, ensuring all sections are submerged.
Incubate for 45 min at 37 °C to degelatinize slides.
Wash slides once with 50 mL of 1× PBS for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Transfer slides to a copling jar containing fresh glycine (Table 2) and incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Transfer slides to a copling jar containing 50 mL of 0.1% triton (Table 2) and permeabilize for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Wash slides with 1× PBS for 5 minutes twice.
Prepare the immunostaining dish with 3 mm paper soaked in 1× PBS.
Dry slides with a tissue all around the slices and place them onto 3 mm paper.
Cover the whole surface of each slide with blocking solution (~0.5 mL per slide) using a Pasteur pipette.
Incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Remove excess blocking solution and dry the slides with a tissue all around the slices.
Place 50 μL of the primary antibody diluted in blocking solution over the sections and cover with coverslips.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C.
Transfer slides to a copling jar containing 50 mL of TBST (Table 2), let the coverslips fall, and wash with TBST for 5 minutes three times.
Place 50 μL of the secondary antibody diluted in blocking solution over the sections and cover with coverslips.
Incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature, protected from light.
Transfer slides to a copling jar and wash with 50 mL of TBST for 5 minutes three times.
Dry the slides with a tissue all around the slices.
Place the slices in a previously prepared immunostaining dish.
Add 0.5 mL of DAPI solution over the whole surface of the slides with a Pasteur pipette.
Incubate for 5 min at RT.
Repeat step 4.4.9.
Carefully dry the slides with a tissue.
Add 50 µL of mounting medium drop by drop along the slide.
Carefully lower a coverslip onto each slide, slightly bending it to avoid bubbles.
